dense_controls.note: capacity planning is analytical via exp_lib.flops_matched_mlp_ratio (run-cfg flops_matched set + flops_match_ref; frozen-config solution mr=689/256=2.69140625); the arm is compute-matched ONLY when the profiler-measured total training FLOPs fall within 1% of the reference — the analytical equality is never the certificate

same-backbone isolation reference (FOLLOWUP mechanism-isolation): q/k RMSNorm + cosine normalization at scale 1.0, the CSA sink, RoPE, and the manual eager sink-attention kernel family — the dense path only takes SDPA when the layer has no sink, so with full_sink=True it shares the CSA kernel family. Remaining deltas ARE the mechanism under test and must stay disclosed: per-token K/V vs the compressed-block KV pipeline, q/k normalization order (dense RMSNorm->RoPE->L2 vs CSA L2->RMSNorm->RoPE), the per-token sliding-window branch, and the projection structure. Capacity is a declared knob, not a fixed one: mr=4 for an unscaled isolation look, or the run-cfg matched set solves parameter equality against the reference sparse arm. It is a system-level isolation reference, never an equal-compute or equal-parameter claim

segmentation_controls.note: cosine-threshold dynamic boundaries with the compression-rate regularizer removed (comp_lambda_mult=0.0): identical architecture/optimizer/data to csa_dynamic_rope with only the reg term zeroed, so dynamic-vs-nocomp isolates what the comp_reg-trained delta_logit offset contributes

the sampled-cut REINFORCE arm (boundary_policy='reinforce'): the ONLY dynamic arm whose discrete boundaries receive a task-loss gradient through exp_lib.boundary_policy_term; the default csa_dynamic_rope stays 'cosine threshold + comp-reg offset' and must never be described as task-learned
the HCA-family twin of csa_dynamic_task (comp_lambda_mult=4.0 as hca_dynamic_rope plus the sampled-cut REINFORCE policy)

rate-matched random boundary placement: content-keyed hash cuts (exp_lib.random_boundary_cut_table, recompute-stable, no RNG stream) with the same target block rate and min/max clamping; no trainable segmentation parameters (dead delta_logit, disclosed like the randidx dead indexer projections) and no compression regularizer (the rate is matched by construction); a nonzero AttnCfg.pattern_seed reruns one training seed under different boundary patterns

reference-boundary control: cuts at the punctuation/eos token positions (exp_lib.boundary_token_ids — the same reference set the boundary-F1 analysis uses); the id set must be registered with model.set_boundary_token_ids(...) before training/evaluation (train_variant boundary_token_ids=...), and re-registered after a checkpoint load (not part of the state dict); a linguistically-motivated upper-REFERENCE, not a claimed-optimal boundary
